name: The Periodic Table
description: Element symbols, atomic numbers, families and the stories behind element names.
question: {prompt}

cards.prompt: What is the chemical symbol for sodium?
cards.fact: Na comes from natrium, the Latin name for sodium.

cards.prompt: What is the chemical symbol for potassium?
cards.fact: K comes from kalium, a Latin name derived from the Arabic for plant ashes.

cards.prompt: What is the chemical symbol for silver?
cards.fact: Ag comes from argentum, Latin for silver — Argentina is named after it too.

cards.prompt: What is the chemical symbol for lead?
cards.fact: Pb comes from plumbum, Latin for lead — the root of the word "plumber".

cards.prompt: What is the chemical symbol for tin?
cards.fact: Sn comes from stannum, the Latin word for tin.

cards.prompt: What is the chemical symbol for tungsten?
cards.fact: W comes from wolfram, the element's German name.

cards.prompt: What is the chemical symbol for copper?
cards.fact: Cu comes from cuprum, Latin for the metal of Cyprus, an ancient copper source.

cards.prompt: What is the chemical symbol for mercury?
cards.fact: Hg comes from hydrargyrum, Greek-derived Latin for "water-silver".

cards.prompt: Which element has the symbol O?
cards.fact: Oxygen makes up about 21% of the air you breathe.

cards.prompt: Which element has the symbol Fe?
cards.fact: Fe comes from ferrum, Latin for iron.

cards.prompt: Which element, symbol Si, is the basis of computer chips?
cards.fact: Silicon Valley takes its name from the silicon chips made there.

cards.prompt: Which element has atomic number 1?
cards.fact: A hydrogen atom is usually just one proton and one electron.

cards.prompt: Which element has atomic number 79?
cards.fact: Gold sits between platinum (78) and mercury (80).

cards.prompt: What is the atomic number of oxygen?
cards.fact: The atomic number counts protons: every oxygen atom has 8.

cards.prompt: What is the atomic number of iron?
cards.fact: The 56 in iron-56 is its mass number; the atomic number, its proton count, is 26.

cards.prompt: What is the atomic number of uranium?
cards.fact: Uranium-238 has 92 protons and 146 neutrons — 238 is its mass number, not its atomic number.

cards.prompt: How many elements have been discovered and officially named (as of 2016)?
cards.fact: The last four — nihonium, moscovium, tennessine and oganesson — were named in 2016.

cards.prompt: Helium, neon and argon belong to which group of elements?
cards.fact: Noble gases have full outer electron shells, so they rarely react with anything.

cards.prompt: Fluorine, chlorine and iodine belong to which group of elements?
cards.fact: Halogen means "salt-former": each one combines with metals to make salts.

cards.prompt: What is the lightest noble gas?
cards.fact: Helium is so light that Earth's gravity can't hold on to it in the upper atmosphere.

cards.prompt: Which gas gives classic signs their red-orange glow?
cards.fact: Other "neon sign" colours usually come from different gases or coloured glass.

cards.prompt: Which radioactive noble gas can build up in basements?
cards.fact: Radon seeps up from uranium decaying in rocks and soil.

cards.prompt: Which element makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere?
cards.fact: Oxygen is only about 21% of the air; argon is nearly 1%.

cards.prompt: What is the most abundant element in Earth's crust?
cards.fact: Oxygen is locked into rocks as silicates and oxides — nearly half the crust by mass.

cards.prompt: Which nonmetal is a liquid at room temperature?
cards.fact: Bromine and mercury are the only elements that are liquid at standard room conditions.

cards.prompt: Which silvery metal melts in your hand, at about 30 °C?
cards.fact: Gallium spoons are a classic prank: they melt in a hot cup of tea.

cards.prompt: Which metal has the highest melting point of all?
cards.fact: Tungsten melts at about 3,422 °C, which is why it made light-bulb filaments.

cards.prompt: Which element is the most electronegative?
cards.fact: Fluorine pulls on electrons harder than any other element, making it fiercely reactive.

cards.prompt: Which element is the backbone of all organic chemistry?
cards.fact: Carbon can form four bonds, letting it build the chains and rings of life.

cards.prompt: Who published the first widely recognised periodic table in 1869?
cards.fact: Mendeleev left gaps for undiscovered elements and correctly predicted their properties.

cards.prompt: Which element is named after Marie and Pierre Curie?
cards.fact: Marie Curie herself discovered polonium and radium.

cards.prompt: Which element did Marie Curie name after her homeland, Poland?
cards.fact: Poland was not an independent country in 1898, so the name was a political statement.

cards.prompt: Which element is named after Albert Einstein?
cards.fact: Einsteinium was first found in the debris of the first hydrogen-bomb test, in 1952.

cards.prompt: Which element is named after the US state where it was first made?
cards.fact: Californium was first made at the University of California, Berkeley, in 1950.

cards.prompt: Helium is named after the Greek word for what?
cards.fact: Helium was spotted in the Sun's spectrum in 1868, decades before it was found on Earth.

cards.prompt: Which element is named after the Moon?
cards.fact: Selene is the Greek Moon goddess; its neighbour tellurium is named after Earth (tellus).

cards.prompt: Which element takes its name from the Greek word for "violet"?
cards.fact: Heated iodine gives off a striking violet vapour.
